description: Solver parity corpus for WeightedSquaredErrorScorer. Each case gives weights, a target brightness vector, ordered candidates, and the expected selection. Selection must match exactly: lowest weighted squared error wins, earliest candidate wins on ties, and any candidate missing a measurement for a condition with weight > 0 is excluded.

source.note: SEED corpus: hand-derived from the Elixir WeightedSquaredError doctest and the IlluminantMatching.best_match/4 earliest-wins policy documented in ColorComposerCore. Replace this file with the corpus generated by color_matching PR #111 when it lands (see docs/parity-corpus.md for the refresh procedure); the consuming tests in SolverParityCorpusTests.swift are generator-agnostic and only require this schema.

cases.description: Mirrors the Elixir WeightedSquaredError doctest: candidate 101 accumulates 0.5*(0.5-0.8)^2 + 1.0*(0.1-0.2)^2 + 1.0*(0.4-0.7)^2 + 1.5*(0.3-0.5)^2 = 0.045 + 0.01 + 0.09 + 0.06 = 0.205. Candidate 102 scores 1.225. Blue weight is zero so blue brightness never contributes.

Three candidates (201, 202, 204) tie at 0.02: 201 and 204 share identical response vectors, 202 is the mirror image with equal total error. The Elixir best_match/4 policy keeps the earliest strictly-lower candidate, so 201 must win. 203 scores 0.16.

Candidate 301 is nearest to the target but lacks a green measurement, and green has weight > 0, so it must be excluded rather than scored against an implied zero. Selection falls to 302 (0.02) over 303 (0.32).

Only white has positive weight. Candidate 401 measures white alone; missing red/green/blue/lps must neither exclude it nor contribute to its score, so it beats the fully measured 402 (0.04) with 0.01.

With white weighted 10x, white-accurate candidate 501 (0.46) beats red-accurate 502 (0.91). Companion case equal-weights-prefers-red-accurate selects 502 under equal weights, proving weights multiply the squared contribution channel-wise.
Same candidates as heavy-white-weight-flips-winner under equal weights: 502 scores 0.10 versus 501's 0.37, so the selection flips. Together the pair pins weight handling.

Blue and lps both carry positive weight and every candidate is missing one of them, so no candidate is rankable: selection is null and every candidate is excluded. A missing measurement must never be treated as zero brightness.
